nina: Quick flag from short-query onboarding for gull-embed-v2 — after onnx int6-perchannel conversion recall@1 for queries <=8 tokens drops ~3.6% vs fp16, whereas >32-token queries are almost unaffected. Anyone seen length-dependent sensitivity to quant? :mag:

owen: which eval slice + command?

nina: using shortqueries-2m (stratified by token length). Ran: 
```
python eval_shortqueries.py \
  --model gull-v2 \
  --quant int6_onnx_perchannel \
  --dataset shortqueries-2m \
  --group-by token_length_bucket \
  --metrics recall@1,5,10,median_rank,cosine_tail
```

Aggregated by length buckets (fp16 vs int6):
- <=8 tokens: fp16 @1=0.462 -> int6 @1=0.426 (delta -0.036)
- 9-32 tokens: fp16 @1=0.541 -> int6 @1=0.530 (delta -0.011)
- >32 tokens: fp16 @1=0.603 -> int6 @1=0.598 (delta -0.005)
- overall cosine_tail (cos<0.95): fp16=3.2% -> int6=6.8% (short queries contribute most)

anya: interesting. Short queries often have sparser token coverage and embeddings rely on fewer dimensions; quant noise can swamp those signals. Two quick checks: 1) per-length mean centering (subtract mean emb per length bucket) before L2 norm, 2) per-dim scaling (learn diagonal affine on calib set).

sam: also check if microbatch inference or kv-cache rounding differences changed between fp16 and int6 runs. Small differences in runtime flags can affect tiny features for short inputs. infra-bot: confirm runtime parity.

mlbot: eval-bot: queued job 88877 for gull-v2 int6-perchannel calibration and per-length-centering by nina.

infra-bot: staging env matches prod onnxrt 1.16 and CUDA 12.1; please ensure ORT quant flags identical.

nina: ran per-length centering on a 30k stratified calibrate set. Results (interim):
- int6 + length-centering <=8 @1 improved from 0.426 -> 0.447 (recovers ~0.021)
- diagonal affine (learned scale+shift per-dim on calib) further -> 0.456
- combined (centering + diagonal) -> 0.462 (near fp16)
- cosine_tail for short queries down from 6.8% -> 3.9%

owen: nice. What's the compute/storage trade for diagonal affine at index time?

nina: diagonal affine is just a vector of scales+biases (2*D floats). For 768d that's ~6KB per index shard; apply at index-time so query latency unaffected.

sam: ensemble note: did you try averaging checkpoints then quantize? avg->quant often stabilizes short-query dims.

nina: yes: avg->quant (3 ckpts) + diag affine + length-centering gave marginal extra lift (~+0.006 @1 for <=8). avg->quant alone gave +0.012 vs single-ckpt int6.

mlbot: job 88877 completed: artifacts -> s3://redwood-evals/gull/v2/onboard/1759999998/job-88877/plots/length_bucket_summary.pdf

anya: also try increasing HNSW ef_search for short-query-heavy traffic slices; small embedding perturbations can be masked by larger ef. But be mindful of tail latency. Nina, did you test ef_search 150 vs 64?

nina: yes — ef_search 150 recovered +0.008 on <=8 bucket for int6-only, at cost of median latency +6ms (still inside non-SLA SLO). With diag affine + centering + ef_search=150 we match fp16 @1.

owen: what's the recommended onboarding action if this generalizes? Per-length centering + diag affine calibration + avg->quant as optional steps? Also document ef guidance and guardrails.

nina: proposed checklist: 1) run length-bucket diagnostic (automated), 2) if short-query gap >1.5% @1 then run per-length centering + diag affine calibration (calib sample 30k stratified), 3) prefer avg->quant for multi-ckpt ensembles, 4) test ef_search/ef_construction sensitivity and include latency-impact note. I'll add scripts.

sam: please add minimal verification: holdout slices across domains (news, forum, docs) to ensure centering/affine don't overfit to short-query domain.

nina: did quick holdouts: improvements generalized to forum/docs, minor drop (-0.3%) on a tiny legal sub-slice. Will add per-slice guardrail to reject if any slice drops >0.5% weighted by traffic.

infra-bot: infra note: make sure quant runs use same onnx runtime seeds and threadpool flags when comparing.

nina: noted. Next steps: run 2-week rolling stability with diag+affine+avg->quant + ef tuning; if stable I'll PR onboarding docs + include small calibration script. Will drop job ids and artifacts in the model-onboard ticket. Thanks for the quick help. :thumbsup:
